data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The 'Reliability Gain' is a phantom of variance reduction; the panel doesn't produce 'better' judgments, but more 'consistent' ones, which only equals reliability if the checklist's mean accuracy is higher than the expert's.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The expert's variance is so high that their 'best' is great but their 'worst' is catastrophic, making the panel's consistency objectively more valuable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is comprehensive enough to cover all possible failure modes of the task.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist converts a high-variance intuitive process into a low-variance algorithmic process. The 'gain' is actually a reduction in the standard deviation of results. To distinguish this from mere compliance, one must introduce a 'Stress Test': a known error NOT on the checklist. If the panel misses it but the expert catches it, the panel's 'reliability' is merely a byproduct of restricted scope.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
